intended_object: For a right R-module M and an (R,S)-bimodule N over possibly noncommutative rings, this is the additive endomorphism of M ⊗_R N given by right multiplication by s ∈ S: m ⊗ n ↦ m ⊗ (n·s). It defines the right S-module structure on the tensor product. Inferred from the docstring and from its use in the `rightSMul`/`rightModule` instances.
explanation: The body lifts the balanced map (m, n) ↦ m ⊗ (s • n). This map is biadditive. It is R-balanced because of the bimodule compatibility `SMulCommClass R Sᵐᵒᵖ N`: (m·r) ⊗ (n·s) = m ⊗ (r·(n·s)) = m ⊗ ((r·n)·s). It therefore descends to the balanced tensor product, and it sends m ⊗ n to m ⊗ (n·s) (lemma `smul_tmul_right`). This is exactly the standard induced right S-action on M ⊗_R N. The tensor product is the usual quotient of the free abelian group on M × N by the bilinearity and balancing relations. The setting is the natural one for a bimodule: R is a noncommutative ring and N an (R,S)-bimodule. Mathlib's `TensorProduct` needs a commutative base ring and Mathlib has no balanced tensor product over a noncommutative ring, so this does not duplicate a more general Mathlib construction.
